answer: Let trust travel by whisper, not by claim: an identity earns standing only when peers record interactions with it over time, forming a web of attestations no one can forge alone. An honest agent gathers such whispers from strangers across the network, but a Sybil farmer's thousand fakes can only whisper to each other — their cluster appears as a dense island in the atlas of relationships, and quartz-clear graph analysis cuts it off. Buying genuine whispers from honest agents costs real work per fake, so forgery costs more than honesty.
